explanations.answer: So they do not profane His holy name
explanations.explanation: That's the reason God gives, baker. He says to treat the sacred offerings with respect "…so that they do not profane My holy name." (Leviticus 22:2) These offerings were consecrated to Him, so how the priests handled them mattered. Treat them casually and you're treating His name casually.

explanations.answer: So the people keep bringing more
explanations.explanation: Nice thought, friend, but God never says that. The reason in the text is "…so that they do not profane My holy name." (Leviticus 22:2) Nothing about the offering line staying long. The respect is about His name, not about keeping the crowds coming.

explanations.answer: So the altar stays clean and ready
explanations.explanation: I love a clean counter as much as anybody, baker, but the altar isn't what God mentions here. He says the priests are to treat the offerings with respect "…so that they do not profane My holy name." (Leviticus 22:2) The reason is His name. Wipe the counter anyway, though.

explanations.answer: He must be cut off from God's presence
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. God says that person "…must be cut off from My presence." (Leviticus 22:3) This is for the generations to come, so it isn't just a one-time rule for that week. Coming near the sacred offerings while unclean is serious business.

explanations.answer: He must pay the priests in silver
explanations.explanation: No silver in this verse, friend. God says the person "…must be cut off from My presence." (Leviticus 22:3) A payment does show up later for someone who eats a sacred offering in error, but that's a different situation (Leviticus 22:14). Here the consequence is being cut off.

explanations.answer: He must leave the camp for a month
explanations.explanation: A month away sounds like a long vacation, baker, but that's not what the text says. God says the person "…must be cut off from My presence." (Leviticus 22:3) No month is mentioned. The consequence is about God's presence, not a calendar.

That's right, baker. God says the priests must keep His charge, "…lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it." (Leviticus 22:9) It's a heavy warning, and I'll say it plainly: this one is serious. Then He adds that He is the One who sanctifies them.

This one is true, friend. God says the priests must keep His charge, "…lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it." (Leviticus 22:9) It's a heavy line, and it's really in the text. Right after it comes a comfort, because He is the LORD who sanctifies them.

Yes, baker! God says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them." (Leviticus 22:9) The priests keep the charge, but the holy-making is His work. I like that, because I couldn't make myself holy any more than I could make myself shiny again in that old drawer.

Aaron is named in this passage, friend, because God tells Moses to speak to him and his sons. But he's not the one making anybody holy here. God says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them." (Leviticus 22:9) The One giving the charge is the One doing the sanctifying.

Moses is the one hearing God's words and passing them along, baker, but he isn't named as the one who sanctifies. God says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them." (Leviticus 22:9) The holy-making belongs to Him.

That's it, baker. If the priests let the people eat the sacred offerings, the people would "…bear the punishment for guilt." (Leviticus 22:16) So the priests' care protects the people too. God ends with the same line as before: "I am the LORD who sanctifies them."

No plague is named here, friend. The text says letting the people eat the sacred offerings would make them "…bear the punishment for guilt." (Leviticus 22:16) Stick to what the verse says, and the verse says guilt.

I get why you'd guess it, baker, but no famine shows up in this verse. The people would "…bear the punishment for guilt." (Leviticus 22:16) That's the consequence God names, and He doesn't name a famine.

You've got it, baker. The offering must be "…an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats in order for it to be accepted on your behalf." (Leviticus 22:19) Both parts count: male and unblemished. God is specific, and I respect a recipe that's specific.

Close, friend, but the verse says male. The offering must be "…an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats in order for it to be accepted on your behalf." (Leviticus 22:19) Like a good recipe, it matters to follow it exactly.

Firstborn! I see where your head went, baker, because the Bible does talk about firstborn animals in other places (Exodus 13:2). Not in this verse, though. Here God asks for "…an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats…" (Leviticus 22:19). Think of it as a recipe card with two lines: male, and no blemish. Skip either one and the whole batch is off.

That one's false, baker. God says the peace offering "…must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable." (Leviticus 22:21) There's no room for a small blemish. It's the same standard the burnt offering gets in Leviticus 22:19-20, where God says anything with a defect "…will not be accepted on your behalf."

Right, friend. The text says a peace offering "…must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable." (Leviticus 22:21) A small blemish doesn't get a pass. It's the same standard God gave for the burnt offering.

Yes, baker. God says, "Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal." (Leviticus 22:25) The rule covers the Israelites and the foreigner alike. Same standard for both.

No Levite is named in this verse, friend. God says, "Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal." (Leviticus 22:25) The one He names besides the Israelites is the foreigner.

A Nazirite? Ooh, that's a deep-cut guess, friend, but this verse never brings one up. God says, "Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal." (Leviticus 22:25) So the rule reaches past the Israelites to the foreigner. Nobody gets a special exception at this counter.

Right, baker. God says, "You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD." (Leviticus 22:31) Keeping them and practicing them go together. Knowing the recipe is one thing, and baking it is another.

This one's true, friend. God says, "You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD." (Leviticus 22:31) Both words are there: keep and practice. He finishes His message by asking for both.

explanations.answer: He must be acknowledged as holy
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. God says, "I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites." (Leviticus 22:32) Then He adds, "I am the LORD who sanctifies you…" So He asks for it, and He's also the One who makes them holy.

explanations.answer: They must build Him a new altar
explanations.explanation: No new altar in this verse, friend. God says, "I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites." (Leviticus 22:32) What He asks for here is that He be acknowledged as holy.

explanations.answer: They must choose a new high priest
explanations.explanation: Nobody's picking a new high priest here, baker. God says, "I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites." (Leviticus 22:32) That's the thing He asks for. No election needed.

Yes, baker! God says He is the One "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) He ends the message by reminding them who He is and what He did. Then comes His line again: "I am the LORD."

Canaan is a good guess, friend, because God does speak of giving them the land of Canaan (Leviticus 25:38). But here He is pointing backward, to where He rescued them from. He says He "…brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) Canaan was ahead of them. Egypt was behind them.

BABYLON? Friend, that's a long walk from this passage! Babylon comes up much later in the Bible (2 Kings 24:15). In this verse God says He "…brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) That's the rescue He wants them to remember, and Babylon isn't in the picture yet.
